news.title: English Wag who cheered Argentina vs Three Lions has Hashtag contract ripped up
news.lede: KELCI-ROSE BOWERS hit the headlines when she turned her back on England during the World Cup – and now she has been cast aside by her club. The defender, 22, is the girlfriend of Marcos Senesi, who joined Tottenham in the summer. And Bowers was in the stands controversially cheering for her partner’s Argentina as Lionel Messi and Co ended England’s World Cup dreams with a stunning semi-final comeback. But the Wag is now preparing to take her own career in another direction after Hashtag United Women ripped up her contract.

news.title: Vikash Dhorasoo says bringing OCI players is interesting, but Indian football should focus on youth structure
news.lede: AIFF Media AIFF Media https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/lp6397/article71534536.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/Vikash%20Dhorasoo.jpg.jpeg AIFF Dhorasoo, who represented France at the FIFA World Cup 2006, said that India playing at the biggest stage would be huge. Chennai Former French midfielder Vikash Dhorasoo said that India’s upcoming friendly against Brazil is a good opportunity for younger players to evaluate how much they need to improve to reach a high level. He said that while bringing overseas players to play for India is good, a lot of the focus in Indian football should be on building a proper youth structure. “I want to insist on the fact that it is not only about bi-national players bringing their talent to the team.

news.title: Salt Lake Stadium: India’s grand football theatre | Football News
news.lede: Kolkata: There are football stadiums that belong to clubs, franchises, and sometimes to a city. And then there is Salt Lake Stadium. For more than four decades, this cauldron has been the place where India’s football has met some of the finest of the world.On Saturday, Brazil will walk out for the first time to play India. Three days later, it will be Uruguay.

news.title: Cubarsi champions defenders' cause but keeps his feet on the ground at home
news.lede: Soccer Football - Spain's Pau Cubarsi Interview - Las Rozas Training Center, Las Rozas, Madrid, Spain - October 1, 2026 Spain's Pau Cubarsi poses for photos during an exclusive interview for Reuters REUTERS/Susana Vera. MADRID, Oct 1 - Pau Cubarsi wants defenders to get their share of football's glittering prizes, but a World Cup winner's medal brings no special privileges at home, where the Barcelona teenager still bickers with his sister over the housework. The 19-year-old Spain centre back is mounting a persuasive challenge to the forwards who usually monopolise individual honours, having played every minute of his country's World Cup triumph and been named the tournament's best young player. He now leads the Golden Boy rankings, chasing an award for Europe's best under-21 player that only one defender, Matthijs de Ligt in 2018, has won since its creation in 2003.

news.title: Yemen and football in the face of civil war: ‘It would be very nice to give the world a different headline’
news.lede: Coach Noureddine Ould Ali is staying positive despite a difficult situation at home and tough opponents at the Gulf Cup. The Yemen national coach, Noureddine Ould Ali, chose not to reach for a good old-fashioned football excuse after his team’s 1-0 loss to Qatar in the Gulf Cup on Saturday, despite a clear penalty not given their way. The defeat meant the Reds crashed out of the eight-team regional tournament, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with a game of the group stage remaining. There are other factors the Algerian could list for a defeat against a team that was at the World Cup.
